quests.contextSentence: I burned myself on the oven door while Dad was chopping vegetables.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'myself' is the first-person reflexive, so it points back to 'I', the speaker. Dad is a third person and would need 'himself'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Myself' can only point back to 'I'. Who is speaking?

quests.contextSentence: 'Please help yourself to a sandwich,' Mrs. Koh told the delivery driver while the children set the table.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yourself' is singular and points to the listener. Mrs. Koh is the speaker, and the children are plural, so it names the driver she is addressing.
quests.nativeTip: 'Yourself' is singular and second person. Who is being spoken to?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'yourself' points back to ➔ 'the delivery driver'

quests.contextSentence: I told myself the delay wasn't Sam's fault and kept my temper.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'myself' is the reflexive partner of 'I'. The speaker is the person who did the telling and the one being told.
quests.nativeTip: Which pronoun in the sentence shows who is talking?

quests.contextSentence: My husband and I booked the tickets ourselves instead of using an agent.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Ourselves' is first-person plural, so it covers the speaker and one other person. That is my husband and I, who did the booking.
quests.nativeTip: 'Ourselves' means 'we'. Who booked?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'ourselves' points back to ➔ 'my husband and I'

quests.contextSentence: Coach Emeka told the players, 'You've only got yourselves to blame for that result.'
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yourselves' addresses more than one listener. Coach Emeka is speaking to the players, so they are 'you'.
quests.nativeTip: 'Yourselves' is plural and second person. Who is being addressed?

quests.contextSentence: 'You two really outdid yourselves with this dinner,' Aunt Rekha told Manoj and Irene.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yourselves' is plural and reflexive. It refers to the two people she is praising, Manoj and Irene, who prepared the meal.
quests.nativeTip: She is speaking to two people. Who are they?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'yourselves' points back to ➔ 'Manoj and Irene'

quests.contextSentence: The old thermostat had reset itself overnight, and Mr. Ochoa had to reprogram it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Consider the form of 'itself': it is a non-human reflexive. The thermostat is the subject that performed and received the reset.
quests.nativeTip: What reset, and what did it reset?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'itself' points back to ➔ 'the old thermostat'

quests.contextSentence: Andre asked Luis to send him the file, but Luis sent himself a copy first.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'himself' refers back to the subject 'Luis', who sent the copy. 'Him' earlier is different: it refers to Andre, the person who asked.
quests.nativeTip: Which person sent something? A reflexive returns to that person.

quests.contextSentence: The applicant described herself as detail-oriented, and the interviewer noted it on the CV.
quests.ruleExplanation: A reflexive refers to the subject of its own clause. The subject of 'described' is the applicant, so 'herself' is the applicant.
quests.nativeTip: Who did the describing?

quests.contextSentence: Ms. Duffy brought her son to the class so that Mr. Ibarra could show him how to protect himself.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'himself' is the object of 'protect' and its subject is 'him', the person being shown. So it is her son, the one being taught.
quests.nativeTip: Who is being taught to protect someone?

quests.contextSentence: The instructions warn users not to lock themselves out of the account by entering the wrong password.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Themselves' returns to the subject of 'lock', which is 'users'. The account and the password cannot lock themselves out in this way.
quests.nativeTip: Who could get locked out?

quests.contextSentence: Mr. Reyes advised the witness to keep herself calm and avoid arguing with the barrister.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Herself' refers to the person who is advised to stay calm, the witness. Mr. Reyes is male, and he is the one giving advice.
quests.nativeTip: Who has to stay calm?

quests.contextSentence: The manager herself signed the cheque, so the accountant didn't need to check it.
quests.ruleExplanation: Remember that 'herself' is an intensive pronoun that stresses who did the signing. It attaches to the manager, the subject of the action.
quests.nativeTip: This 'herself' adds emphasis. Who signed?

quests.contextSentence: I don't need a repair service; I can fix the tap myself.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Myself' emphasises that the speaker does the repair, not a service. It belongs to 'I'.
quests.nativeTip: Who says they can do the job?

quests.contextSentence: The city council itself admitted that the report contained errors.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Itself' stresses who made the admission. A council can admit things; a report cannot.
quests.nativeTip: Who admitted something?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'itself' points back to ➔ 'the city council'

quests.contextSentence: Farah asked Iris to send her the invoice.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'her' is an ordinary object pronoun, so it points to a different person from the one sending, Iris. The person to receive the invoice is Farah.
quests.nativeTip: If it meant Iris, English would use 'herself'. Who wants the invoice?

quests.contextSentence: Theo hurt himself moving the sofa, and his roommate drove him to the clinic.
quests.ruleExplanation: The subject of 'drove' is the roommate, so an ordinary object 'him' cannot mean him. It points to Theo, who was injured.
quests.nativeTip: Who drove, and who was driven?

quests.contextSentence: Ms. Kruger told the trainees to introduce themselves to the team and tell them about the project.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Themselves' returns to the trainees, but a plain 'them' should point to someone else. That is the team who hear about the project.
quests.nativeTip: 'Themselves' is the trainees. Is 'them' the same group?

quests.contextSentence: Karim and Jonas taught themselves guitar from online videos.
quests.ruleExplanation: Here, 'themselves' is plural, so it needs both names. Karim and Jonas are the subject of 'taught' and the ones who learned.
quests.nativeTip: 'Themselves' is plural. How many people learned?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'themselves' points back to ➔ 'Karim and Jonas'

quests.contextSentence: The neighbours and I have set ourselves a goal of planting fifty trees this year.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Ourselves' is first person, so it includes the speaker. It refers to the neighbours and I together, since we set the goal.
quests.nativeTip: 'Ourselves' includes the speaker. Who is 'we'?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'ourselves' points back to ➔ 'the neighbours and I'

quests.contextSentence: Anisha and her cousin wrapped the gifts themselves, then asked the shop to deliver them.
quests.ruleExplanation: In this sentence, 'themselves' is plural and stresses who did the work. It refers to the two who wrapped, not the shop that delivers.
quests.nativeTip: Who did the wrapping?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'themselves' points back to ➔ 'Anisha and her cousin'

quests.contextSentence: Anjali bought a small gift for herself and a larger one for her mother.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Herself' returns to the subject of 'bought', so it is Anjali. Her mother is the second beneficiary.
quests.nativeTip: Who is the buyer?

quests.contextSentence: Tomás kept the last slice for himself, not for his guests.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'himself' follows the preposition 'for' and refers back to the subject, Tomás. The contrast 'not for his guests' confirms it.
quests.nativeTip: Who kept the slice?

quests.contextSentence: The chairperson listened while the committee members argued among themselves about the budget.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Themselves' is plural and returns to the subject of 'argued'. The chairperson is singular and is only listening.
quests.nativeTip: Who was arguing?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'themselves' points back to ➔ 'the committee members'

quests.contextSentence: Please book yourself a slot online, or ask the front desk to do it for you.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Yourself' addresses the reader, the person the sign is written for. The front desk is only an alternative helper.
quests.nativeTip: Who is the notice speaking to?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'yourself' points back to ➔ 'the person reading'

quests.contextSentence: Users must identify themselves with a passcode before the system lets them in.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Themselves' returns to the subject 'users', who are the ones who must identify. The system is singular.
quests.nativeTip: Who has to identify?

quests.contextSentence: The unit is designed to protect itself from overheating by slowing its fan.
quests.ruleExplanation: Look closely: 'itself' is a non-human reflexive. The unit is the subject of the whole sentence and is the thing protected.
quests.nativeTip: What is being protected?

quests.contextSentence: Ms. Igwe asked the two interns to prepare the slides themselves, since the designer was on leave.
quests.ruleExplanation: The pronoun 'themselves' is plural and emphasises who will do the task. Ms. Igwe and the designer are single people.
quests.nativeTip: Who is going to prepare the slides?
quests.visualAnchor: 🔗 Pronoun 'themselves' points back to ➔ 'the two interns'

quests.contextSentence: After the accident, Dario blamed himself, but his brother told him it wasn't his fault.
quests.ruleExplanation: 'Told him' has 'his brother' as its subject, so 'him' is someone else. It is Dario, who was blaming himself.
quests.nativeTip: Who is being told, and who is doing the telling?

quests.contextSentence: Reza asked himself whether the quote was reasonable, then showed it to his brother-in-law, who runs a garage.
quests.ruleExplanation: Note that 'it' is the object of 'showed' and must be something that can be judged and shown. The quote is what he was weighing up, while the brother-in-law and the garage are people and places.
quests.nativeTip: What was he questioning, and then showed to someone?
